title: Grading and Road Construction
body: Left alone, high spots and rough switchbacks don't stay small problems — they crack tires, shift payload, and turn ramp turns into the site's most common incident location because trucks lose visibility and traction right when they need it most.
keyPoints: High spots on haul roads, benches, or ramps cause uneven truck loading and shift payload over time if not graded out — treat them as a priority, not a routine chore.
Switchbacks need extra grading attention: super-elevation (banking), inside-radius clearance, and outside bund integrity. Most ramp incidents happen at switchbacks, not straight sections.
No unsupervised grading parallel to a high wall inside the 10 m no-go zone — the high-wall exclusion rule always overrides the grading task at hand.
Diff lock goes on when grading, but never make sharp turns with it engaged.

If a road surface is hardened past the point grading can fix — the girl is cutting but nothing changes — that's a base-material problem, not a profile problem. It needs soft material mixed in, not more grader passes.
apply: When you're on the ramps, don't just eyeball the straights — check the switchback turns specifically for banking and bund integrity, since that's where a graded-but-still-hard surface will bite a truck first.
